cells.tense: The decisions are landing clean, and they're landing while you're still with someone.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: This week, when you're sure of something and someone near you is sure of the opposite, hold both without deciding which wins. Let it sit overnight. If the answer arrives by itself, fine.
cells.core:
You see what's needed and act on it before it turns into a speech, and people catch up in their own time. This is the mark of it going well: nothing needs an audience or a defense, and the room feels the clarity anyway. The gap between seeing and saying is short, and it's yours.

Your next edge isn't more certainty. It's sitting with something you know without laying it on the table yet, especially with people you're close to. That's not doubt. It's the difference between knowing a thing and needing to be seen knowing it. Try it once this week and notice what shifts in the talk when nobody has to agree.
cells.sheetLine: You know it before you say it, and that's enough.
cells.verb: moving with a clarity that doesn't need to announce itself
cells.place: beside other people, where feeling-with happens

cells.tense: You'll have already decided how it goes before the person across from you finishes their sentence.
cells.act: cut through the story to what actually follows
cells.ask: With one person, take the story they're telling and work out what actually follows from the facts. Say that part back, then leave room for them to say what comes next.
cells.core:
In a good week your certainty settles a room. People bring you the thing they can't sort out, because you hear it once and the shape of it is plain, and you hand it back smaller than they gave it. That still happens. It's just running ahead of them now.

You finish their thought, and you're often right, and something in them closes anyway, because being read isn't the same as being met. Cut to what's actually true in what they said rather than to what you see coming. The facts on the table can't wait; the certainty about where this lands can. What follows still follows, on their feet.
cells.sheetLine: Being right about the ending can cost you the person.

cells.tense: There was a clearing once, and you've been standing at the edge of it, not building.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: From something you dropped, pick the smallest piece of what comes after. A message. A shelf. A first payment. Make that piece real this week.
cells.core:
You're the steadiest thing in a gathering when this is upright — people bring you what's falling apart and leave with something that holds. That part of you is still here. What's around you is the open ground after a clearing: some setup or obligation or way of being with people stopped working, and the space it left is wide and bare.

Don't try to feel connected a certain way. You can't push a feeling into a place that's gone quiet, and it won't fill. Put something up on the cleared ground instead — one small true thing, made with your hands, that the new life needs to stand on. What holds your people later starts with what you raise now.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing is done. Build the small thing before you feel ready.

cells.tense: Something keeps steady in this circle, and the way you tell it, it keeps steady by nobody in particular.
cells.ask: Keep steadying this group the way you already do, and while you do it, know that you're doing it. No announcement, no credit. If someone asks, you can say it was you, or say nothing.
cells.core:
When the group settles because you're in it, and the thing that matters gets remembered, and people trust the ground under them without knowing why — that's the good face of this. It's already working. The only piece missing is that you don't count yourself as the one carrying it.

Asked, you'd say it runs without anyone steering. Next time you steady something here, know you're doing it as you do it: the plain fact in your own head, nothing spoken. Knowing isn't a claim, and it doesn't change the work. It only puts your name back where the effort already is.
cells.sheetLine: It holds steady, and your hands are the ones holding it.
